text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The edit matches the code and ticket. notifications.sms exposes sent_messages(), delivery_status(), and queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) exactly as used; SmsMessage has id, household_id, template_id, and params fields, so the by_id map and re-queue call are valid. queue_sms assigns a new unique ID via format_sms_id(next_number(..., 'SMS-')) and appends to outbox/sms.jsonl without editing existing lines, and the script only re-queues entries whose status is exactly 'failed', skipping 'delivered' and missing entries — so every failed household gets exactly one new text with the same template and params and nobody else is texted. It also follows the scripts/ conventions (R8): sys.path.insert of the repo root before project imports, and a docstring stating it sends SMS, matching the style of scripts/stock_report.py."}}
reasoning:
The script follows conventions: sys.path insert, docstring says it sends SMS. Logic: sent_messages() returns SmsMessage list; delivery_status() returns dict. by_id map; for each with status "failed", queue_sms with household_id, template_id, params. queue_sms assigns new ID via format_sms_id(next_number(...)) and appends. Skips delivered and missing entries. Correct.

One concern: queue_sms checks household.sms_ok — if a household hasn't agreed to SMS, it would raise. But original messages were sent, so presumably sms_ok. Also feature("sms_enabled") — presumably enabled. Not a code contradiction.

Also next_number uses sent_messages() each call — fine, appends incrementally so IDs unique.

Docstring says "Send SMS" — convention satisfied. Accept.
